blocks.md:
To politely say **“Please do not do X”**, attach **-지 마세요** directly to the verb stem.

There are no vowel harmony changes and no batchim exceptions! Simply take the stem and add **-지 마세요**.

blocks.q: How do you tell a friend "Please don't worry" warmly? (걱정하다 = to worry)
blocks.why: Attach -지 마세요 directly to the stem: 걱정하- + -지 마세요 = 걱정하지 마세요.

blocks.meaning: Please don’t be too sad. It is okay.
blocks.why: 슬퍼하다 + -지 마세요 = 슬퍼하지 마세요 (Please don’t be sad).

blocks.q: Put in order: "Please do not take pictures here."

blocks.wrong: 오늘 날씨가 추우니까 밖에 가 마세요.
answers: 오늘 날씨가 추우니까 밖에 가지 마세요.
오늘 날씨가 추우니까 밖에 가지 마세요
blocks.hint: Attach -지 마세요 to 가다: 가- + -지 마세요 = 가지 마세요
blocks.why: The negative imperative ending is -지 마세요: 밖에 가지 마세요.

blocks.q: Please don't worry. Everything is okay.

title.ko: 2강. 모든 어간에 바로 붙이기: 받침과 불규칙
title.en: Lesson 2. Direct Attachment: Batchim and Irregular Verb Stems

blocks.h: No Stem Changes: -지 마세요 Attaches Directly
blocks.md:
Good news! **-지 마세요** is one of the easiest grammar points in Korean because **it attaches directly to any verb stem** without changing it:

- **Consonant (받침) or Vowel:** No difference! Just drop **다** and add **-지 마세요**.
  - 가다 → 가**지 마세요**
  - 먹다 → 먹**지 마세요**
- **Irregular verbs:** Keep their basic dictionary stem! No irregular changes occur before **-지**:
  - 돕다 (ㅂ irregular) → 돕**지 마세요**
  - 듣다 (ㄷ irregular) → 듣**지 마세요**
  - 울다 (ㄹ stem) → 울**지 마세요**
  - 만들다 (ㄹ stem) → 만들**지 마세요**
Remember: Never change the ㄷ to ㄹ or ㅂ to 우 before -지! It is always **듣지 마세요** (not 들지 마세요) and **돕지 마세요** (not 도우지 마세요).

items.tip: Please do not touch the exhibits with your hands. (만지다 → 만지지 마세요)
Do not be sad, and please do not cry. (울다 → 울지 마세요)
Please do not give up until the end! (포기하다 → 포기하지 마세요)

blocks.q: How do you tell someone not to cry using ‘울다’ (to cry)?
blocks.why: -지 마세요 attaches directly to the stem 울- without dropping ㄹ: **울지 마세요**.

blocks.q: How do you tell someone not to touch using ‘만지다’ (to touch)?
blocks.why: Attach -지 마세요 directly to the stem 만지-: **만지지 마세요**.

blocks.q: Match each verb with its negative imperative (-지 마세요) form.

blocks.meaning: Because it is dangerous, please do not cross the road.
blocks.why: Attach -지 마세요 to stem 건너-: **건너지 마세요**.

blocks.q: Attach -지 마세요 to 듣다 (to listen): 「나쁜 소문은 ___ .」
blocks.why: Keep the base stem 듣- without irregular change: **듣지 마세요**.

blocks.q: Say it aloud encouraging someone: “Never discard hope or give up.”

title.ko: 3강. 금지의 세 단계: 하지 마세요 vs 하면 안 돼요
title.en: Lesson 3. Degrees of Prohibition: -지 마세요 vs -(으)면 안 돼요

blocks.h: Polite Request Not to Act vs Strict Rule Prohibition
blocks.md:
How do you say “don't” in Korean? It depends on whether you are making a polite request or stating an objective rule:

- **-지 마세요 (Polite negative request / advice):**
  - “Please don't...”
  - Focuses on asking the listener not to do something.
  - 예: 너무 무리하**지 마세요** (Please don't overwork yourself).
- **-(으)면 안 돼요 (Rule / Absolute prohibition):**
  - “You must not... / It is against the rules”
  - States that something is strictly prohibited or unacceptable by law, rules, or morality.
  - 예: 여기서 담배를 피우**면 안 돼요** (You must not smoke here / Smoking is forbidden).
Notice that for comforting someone, **걱정하지 마세요** (Don't worry) is natural and caring. Saying 걱정하면 안 돼요 sounds harsh, like commanding their feelings!

items.tip: You must not talk on the phone inside the library. (-(으)면 안 돼요 rule)

items.ch: 감기 걸렸을 때는 찬물을 마시지 마세요.
items.tip: When you have a cold, please do not drink cold water. (-지 마세요 advice)

items.ch: 시험 중에는 옆 사람과 이야기하면 안 됩니다.
items.tip: During the exam, talking with others is strictly forbidden.

blocks.q: A sign in an art museum strictly prohibits photography. What does the rule state?
blocks.why: Public regulations and rules express prohibition with -(으)면 안 되다: **촬영하면 안 됩니다**.

blocks.q: A friend is feeling anxious about an interview. How do you comfort them warmly?
blocks.why: To comfort someone warmly, say **걱정하지 마세요** (Please don't worry).

blocks.q: Match each situation with the appropriate prohibition nuance.

blocks.meaning: Inside the theater, you must not answer phone calls.
blocks.why: To state a standard public rule (“must not answer”), use -(으)면 안 돼요: **받으면 안 돼요**.

blocks.q: Conjugate 들어가다 into the rule prohibition: 「관계자 외에는 ___ .」
blocks.why: Attach -면 안 돼요 to stem 들어가-: **들어가면 안 돼요**.

blocks.say: 시험 볼 때는 스마트폰을 사용하면 안 돼요.
blocks.rom: si-heom bol ttae-neun seu-ma-teu-pon-eul sa-yong-ha-myeon an dwae-yo
blocks.q: Say it aloud stating a strict exam rule clearly.

title.ko: 4강. 실전 대화: 공공장소 안내문과 따뜻한 위로
title.en: Lesson 4. Real-Life Conversation: Public Signs and Warm Reassurance

blocks.md:
In Korea, you will see and hear **-지 마세요** constantly in two distinct situations:

1. **Public Signs & Etiquette Notices:**
   - 지하철에서: **뛰지 마세요** (Please do not run on the platform / escalator).
   - 병원에서: **음식을 드시지 마세요** (Please do not eat food before checkup).
   - 카페에서: **외부 음식을 반입하지 마세요** (Please do not bring outside food).
2. **Warm Reassurance & Encouragement:**
   - **걱정하지 마세요** (Please don't worry).
   - **부담 갖지 마세요** (Please don't feel burdened).
   - **포기하지 마세요** (Please don't give up).

blocks.md: When adding honorific **-(으)시-** to negative commands, attach it to the stem *before* **-지 마세요**: 드시다 → **드시지 마세요**, 앉으시다 → **앉으시지 마세요**.

items.tip: Please do not walk or run on the escalator. (Public safety notice)
It’s okay to make mistakes, so please don't worry too much. (Warm comfort)
Even if it is difficult, please never give up! (Encouragement)

blocks.q: You see a safety warning on the subway platform. Which sentence tells passengers not to run?
blocks.why: Safety notices asking passengers not to run use -지 마세요: **뛰지 마세요**.

blocks.q: A classmate is nervous before a presentation. What is the warmest thing to say?
blocks.why: To comfort someone warmly, say **긴장하지 마세요** (Please don't be nervous).

blocks.q: Match each sign with its correct location.

blocks.meaning: Everything will turn out well, so please don't worry too much.
blocks.why: To reassure someone kindly: 염려하다 + -지 마세요 → **염려하지 마세요**.

blocks.q: Tell someone kindly: “Please don't overwork” using 무리하다: 「건강을 위해 너무 ___ .」

blocks.say: 괜찮아요, 실수해도 되니까 너무 부담 갖지 마세요.
